title: Compatible flat base-change section diagrams on finite intersections of quasi-compact opens
statement:
Let $R\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $X=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $g:X\to Y$ be its projection. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens of $Y$. Let $J$ be the nonempty finite subsets of $I$, ordered by inclusion, and put $V_F=\bigcap_{i\in F}U_i$ and $W_F=g^{-1}(V_F)$ for $F\in J$. Then $J$ is directed, $X$ is quasi-separated, and all $V_F$ and $W_F$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated open subschemes. Put $A_F=\Gamma(V_F,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $B_F=\Gamma(W_F,\mathcal O_X)$, with their $R$-algebra and $T$-algebra structures induced by the structure morphisms [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. For $F\subseteq G$, let $a_{FG}:A_F\to A_G$ and $b_{FG}:B_F\to B_G$ be restriction. The canonical $T$-algebra maps [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]
$$\varphi_F:A_F\otimes_RT\longrightarrow B_F,\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto (g|_{W_F})^\sharp(u)\,t$$
are isomorphisms and satisfy
$$\varphi_G\circ(a_{FG}\otimes1)=b_{FG}\circ\varphi_F.$$
In particular they define an isomorphism of directed diagrams of $T$-algebras. These maps use the identification of the open subscheme $W_F$ with $V_F\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}T$ and the ordinary restriction maps of the structure sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0APJ, lemma-affine-base-change proof: finite-intersection refinement and the corresponding result for quasi-compact opens and their inverse images

proof.text: Choose $i\in I$. Then $\{i\}\in J$, and for $F,G\in J$ their union $F\cup G\in J$ contains both. Thus $J$ is a small nonempty directed poset. For $F\subseteq G$ one has $V_G\subseteq V_F$ and $W_G\subseteq W_F$; restrictions therefore point in the displayed direction. Identity and composition of restriction are the presheaf identities.

source.place: Tag 0APJ, lemma-affine-base-change, first two sentences of the proof; explicit finite-subset refinement

proof.text: The quasi-separated-space condition identified by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] says that intersections of compact opens are compact. Iterate it over each nonempty finite set of indices; Mathlib packages this iteration as QuasiSeparatedSpace.isCompact_sInter_of_nonempty. The range of the finite nonempty index subtype is finite and nonempty, and every member is an open compact subset by hypothesis. Opens.coe_iInf identifies its intersection with V_F. An open embedding into a quasi-separated space has quasi-separated domain (Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.quasiSeparatedSpace), giving quasi-separatedness of every open subscheme.

source.place: Tag 01KO, lemma-characterize-quasi-separated, (1) implies (2) and (3) implies (1); finite affine cover argument

proof.text: The map Spec T to Spec R is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Its base change g is affine, quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The qcqs permanence theorem [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] gives quasi-separatedness of X and compactness of the inverse images W_F. Each W_F is quasi-separated by its open embedding in X. No separately constructed isomorphism between an inverse-image open and a fibre product is required: the open-section version of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] applies directly to the chosen cartesian square and the opens.

Apply Mathlib isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right, the recorded declaration of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs], to the cartesian square with opens top, top, V_F and W_F. This makes the section square a ring pushout. Transport the base and right vertices by the spectrum section isomorphisms GammaSpecIso R and GammaSpecIso T [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; their naturality identifies the base morphism with r. Compare this pushout with the standard tensor-product pushout [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The composite comparison is a ring isomorphism. The equations on the two coprojections imply that a tensor 1 tensor t maps to the structural image of t, so this ring isomorphism respects T and upgrades to a T-algebra isomorphism. Factor a pure tensor as (a tensor 1)(1 tensor t); multiplicativity and the coprojection equations give precisely the displayed formula.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (2), degree zero and structure sheaf; used in Tag 0APJ

proof.text: For $F\subseteq G$ and $u\in A_F$, naturality of the structure-sheaf map of the morphism $g$ [def-pc-scheme] gives $b_{FG}((g|_{W_F})^\sharp(u))=(g|_{W_G})^\sharp(a_{FG}(u))$. The structural section of $t\in T$ on $W_F$ restricts to its structural section on $W_G$. Hence on $u\otimes t$ both composites in the asserted square give $(g|_{W_G})^\sharp(a_{FG}(u))t$. These computations in particular agree on $u\otimes1$ and $1\otimes t$, so the tensor-product uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](3) proves equality of the two algebra maps. Restriction composition and identity give the two diagrams. The squares just proved give a natural transformation with components $\varphi_F$; multiplying each square by the component inverses gives naturality of $(\varphi_F^{-1})_F$. Thus this is an isomorphism of directed diagrams.
